holder.name: Taufa'ahau Tupou IV
holder.note: King when the period opens: dated royal assents of 12 July and 8 August 1990 (TO-CROWN-01). His reign ended with his death in Auckland at 00:34 on 11 September 2006, Tongan time (23:34 on 10 September, New Zealand time), as Gazette No. 20 records; Gazette No. 19 states that the Crown devolved by his decease (TO-CROWN-03, TO-CROWN-04).
holder.uncertainty: The start of the reign (1965) is outside the period and is not structured. The end is the Tongan calendar date of the death, to which the proclamation's devolution wording ties the transfer of the Crown; it is not taken from George Tupou V's proclamation or coronation. The State Funeral, burial and mourning are separate claims.

holder.name: George Tupou V
holder.note: Formerly Crown Prince Tupouto'a; Siaosi Tupou V in the Tongan texts. Accession by devolution of the Crown on the decease of Taufa'ahau Tupou IV at 00:34 on 11 September 2006, Tongan time (TO-CROWN-04); proclaimed King by Gazette No. 19 on the same Tongan day, as a separate event. Traditional installation (taumafa kava) on 30 July 2008 and coronation on 1 August 2008 (TO-CROWN-05). Died in Hong Kong at 20:58 on 18 March 2012, Tonga time (TO-CROWN-06).
holder.uncertainty: The start is the stated devolution on his predecessor's death, not the proclamation, the traditional installation, the coronation or the coronation oath (which no source dates). The end is his death as Gazette Extraordinary No. 8 records it; Gazette Extraordinary No. 9 states that the Crown devolved by his decease. No accession time is stored.

fictional_people.name: Lesieli Fotu
fictional_people.fictional_biography: An invented secondary-school science teacher from an outer-island village of Vava'u who later coordinated a women's handicraft and fisheries cooperative and a solar-lighting programme for remote households. In play she may register as an elector in a Vava'u constituency and stand, formally as an individual, when a general election or by-election occurs. She holds a people's seat only if she wins one in play.
fictional_people.restriction: A gameplay institutional event is required; these invented people never replace an incumbent because a date passes.

fictional_people.name: Sitani Lolohea
fictional_people.fictional_biography: An invented civil engineer who managed road and water-supply works across Tongatapu and later ran a small construction-safety training business. In play he may first win a Tongatapu people's seat at a general election or by-election. Only as a sitting elected representative could he be nominated, seconded by two other elected representatives, and recommended by a majority in a secret ballot for appointment as Prime Minister.
fictional_people.restriction: A gameplay institutional event is required; these invented people never replace an incumbent because a date passes.

fictional_people.name: Pisila Tukuafu
fictional_people.fictional_biography: An invented public-finance specialist who managed budget-reform programmes for a regional development organisation in the Pacific and later taught public administration at a tertiary institute in Nuku'alofa. In play a Prime Minister could nominate her as one of the few Cabinet Ministers who are not elected representatives; she would take a ministry only after formal appointment by the King on that nomination. She would sit and vote in the Assembly, but not in a vote of no confidence, and would retain office until a constitutionally defined termination. After a general election she would remain a caretaker until her appointment is revoked or continued on the incoming Prime Minister's recommendation; the election date alone does not remove her.
fictional_people.restriction: A gameplay institutional event is required; these invented people never replace an incumbent because a date passes.

fictional_people.name: Kalolo Matalehu
fictional_people.fictional_biography: An invented community-radio producer and youth rugby coach from a village in eastern Tongatapu who later managed a small printing and publishing cooperative. In play he may join a political organization such as the Democratic Party of the Friendly Islands (PTOA) after the fictional window opens and be chosen as its leader only under that organization's own rules, if its leadership falls vacant. Leading it would not give him a seat: he would still need to win a people's constituency as an individual candidate.
